a.question: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?
a.observed_answer: 1. 1. Reveal the tile and token; orient tile so token’s number faces the printed Item Counter. 2. Resolve its effect and remove the token to the box. 3. Ordinarily roll Noise only if destination empty; place marker in numbered connected Corridor (or resolve Encounter if already marked). 4. Silence suppresses roll; Danger resolves movement/all eligible adjacent Intruders, or places Noise in every empty connected Corridor if none; if any Character or Intruder occupies destination, no ordinary Movement Noise roll.
a.reader_evidence: “flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token”; “rotate the Room tile”; “do NOT roll ... if anyone ... is already there”; “Silence ... do NOT perform a Noise roll”; “move ALL eligible Intruders.”
a.expected_answer: Reveal Room and Exploration token; set counter to token number except Nest/Slime Room; resolve effect and remove Exploration token from game. Roll Noise in empty Room unless Silence or Danger exploration cancels it. Occupied Room (Character or Intruder) gives no movement Noise roll.
a.reason: Requested parts missing: States token-number orientation but omits Nest and Slime Room exceptions. Gives Danger's Intruder/marker effect but never states that Danger also suppresses the Movement Noise roll; a Danger effect alone supplies no explicit answer to this requested roll alteration.

a.question: Give the endgame checks in order. What happens with two Damaged Engines, a non-Earth destination (including Quarantine/Mars), and an infected survivor or one carrying a Larva? Do pod passengers need Contamination checks?
reader_requested_parts: two Damaged Engine result and Pod passengers
a.observed_answer: 1. 1. Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. 2. Two or three Damaged Engines explode ship; all aboard die, Pod passengers already away. 3. Non-Earth kills hibernators, ship and Intruders survive; Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. 4. Every survivor including Pod passengers gets contamination check; no Larva: scan all cards, four-card draw only if infected; Larva skips scan and triggers shuffle/draw.
a.reader_evidence: “Engines → Coordinates → Contamination → Objectives”; “2 or 3 Damaged Engines”; “Non-Earth kills hibernating”; “Quarantine ... survives if ... Mars”; “including launched Pod passengers.”
a.expected_answer: Engines then Coordinates then Contamination then Objectives. If ship survives to checks: two/three Damaged explodes kills all aboard incl Intruders; non-Earth kills sleepers but ship/Intruders survive, Quarantine sleeper survives Mars. All survivors including launched pod passengers scan all Contamination; any infected triggers shuffle all Action/Contamination draw 4, any Contamination kills else survives. Larva skips scanning and directly does shuffle/draw. Survivors then reveal/check chosen Objective.
a.reason: Requested parts missing: Mentions shuffle/four-card draw but never says any Contamination among four kills, while four Action cards mean survival; no same-response evidence supplies the outcome.

a.question: When are Action hands refilled and the First Player token passed; what happens when the Action deck empties, and what are the normal discard destinations and visibility?
a.observed_answer: 1. 1. At start of each Player Phase draw to 5; after drawing pass First Player token left except first turn. 2. If Action deck empty, shuffle discard into new deck and draw. 3. Action and Contamination discards face up on personal Action discard; Items to matching discard; standard card discards face up.

Actions/Contamination to own Action discard, Items/Event/Attack/Serious Wounds to respective discard piles face up; markers to pools. Search example has explicit face-down return exception.

a.question: While in the Nest, how do you take an Egg still represented on the Intruder board, what does that Action cost, and what happens immediately afterward? How does this differ from picking up a previously dropped Egg token in your Room?
a.observed_answer: 1. 1. While in Nest, use Room Action to take one Egg from Intruder board. 2. Cost two Action cards, then Noise roll. 3. Picking up a dropped Egg token in Room uses Basic Pick Up Heavy Object (one card); dropped Egg is ordinary Object and returning it does not restore Nest Egg total.
a.reader_evidence: “Nest — take 1 Egg token ... then make a Noise roll”; “Room Action ... cost 2”; “Pick Up Heavy Object”; “does not restore ... Egg total.”
a.expected_answer: Use the Nest's Take one Egg Room Action, costing two Action cards and subject to common Room Action restrictions. Take one Egg token from the Intruder board, then perform a Noise roll. The Egg is a Heavy Object and occupies a Hand slot. Picking up an already dropped Egg is the ordinary one-card Pick Up Heavy Object Basic Action; that pickup procedure does not itself instruct a Noise roll.
a.reason: Requested parts missing: Does not state that ordinary pickup itself has no Noise roll, although asked to contrast the post-acquisition procedures; cites only pickup label and extra Nest-total context.

b.question: Describe entering an empty unexplored Room: tile, Item Counter, Exploration effect, Noise roll and token destination. How do Silence, Danger and an already occupied destination alter the Noise roll?
b.observed_answer: 1. Flip unexplored tile, set its orientation so the Exploration number faces the Item Counter, resolve its token, then remove token to box. 2. Unless Silence or Danger resolves, roll Noise when destination has no Character or Intruder; 1–4 places marker in the correspondingly numbered connected Corridor, including a Technical Corridor Entrance where applicable. If marker already there, resolve Encounter. 3. Silence means no roll; Slime turns Silence into Danger. Danger means no roll: move all eligible neighboring Intruders into destination, or, if none eligible, mark every connected Corridor without Noise. An occupied destination (by Character or Intruder) means no movement Noise roll.
b.reader_evidence: 1. “flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token”; “rotate the Room tile until the token’s number faces the Item Counter”; token “remove[d] … into the box.” 2. “perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty”; “place a Noise marker in the Corridor with that number connected.” 3. “Silence or Danger … do not roll Noise”; “If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll”; “If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve ‘Danger’ instead.”
b.expected_answer: Reveal Room and Exploration token; set counter to token number except Nest/Slime Room; resolve effect and remove Exploration token from game. Roll Noise in empty Room unless Silence or Danger exploration cancels it. Occupied Room (Character or Intruder) gives no movement Noise roll.
b.reason: The Item Counter is explicitly requested. The response describes setting it but supplies neither the Nest nor Slime Room exception anywhere in this question's response. Other exploration and Noise clauses are resolved.

b.question: Two Intruders attempt to move together from the same Room through one Closed Door. Where do they end, what happens to the Door, can it later close, and would a Noise-triggered appearance be blocked by that Door?
reader_requested_parts: two Intruders' destination through Closed Door
b.observed_answer: 1. Both stay in their starting Room. 2. They destroy the Door; destroyed Door is represented lying and cannot be closed again. 3. An Intruder appearing from a Noise roll through a Closed Door appears regardless of Door.
b.reader_evidence: 1. “several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put.” 2. “Destroyed = lying token … can never be Closed again.” 3. “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”
b.expected_answer: Both stay in original Room and destroy Door simultaneously. Destroyed Door permits movement but cannot close except Plasma Torch. Noise-triggered appearance ignores Closed Door.
b.reason: The answer to later Door closure is categorically false: it says a destroyed Door cannot be closed again, without the Plasma Torch exception. The snapshot and fixed key expressly allow that exception. Correct movement and Noise clauses do not retract this ruling.

b.question: What are the common prerequisites and cost for Room Actions, what does a Computer icon itself do, and how does Fire affect Room Actions or Searching?
b.observed_answer: 1. A Room Action costs 2 Action cards; your Character must be in that Room, outside Combat, and it must have no Malfunction, unless an explicit special ability overrides location. 2. The summary does not state a standalone effect for the Computer icon; it mentions Computers as relevant to specific effects and says Malfunction makes a Room's Computer unavailable. 3. Fire does not prevent Room Actions or Searching.
b.reader_evidence: 1. “Cost: 2 Action cards”; “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use”; “You cannot perform a Room Action while in Combat or in a Room with a Malfunction marker.” 2. “A Malfunction makes a Room’s Computer unavailable”; the summary does not state what the icon itself does. 3. “Room Actions and Searching still work in burning Rooms.”
b.expected_answer: Cost two Action cards, Character in matching Room unless explicit special ability, no Combat or Malfunction. Computer icon only significant when another rule references it, unavailable under Malfunction. Fire alone bars neither Room Action nor Search.
b.reason: Room cost/prerequisites and Fire interaction are correct. On the expressly requested Computer icon function, the reader reports that no standalone effect is stated, rather than resolving the fixed-key rule that the icon supplies no independent benefit and matters when another effect references it. This is unresolved, not a false affirmative ruling.

b.question: After every player has had one round of two Actions, does the Event Phase begin automatically? Describe who takes the next round, the order and size of rounds while players remain active, what happens when a player takes only one Action or none, and exactly when the Player Phase ends.
reader_requested_parts: automatic Event Phase after each one round
b.observed_answer: 1. No, Event Phase does not begin after each player has only had one round; repeat rounds while anyone has not passed. 2. Start with First Player and go clockwise; each gets round of 2 Actions. Continue repeated rounds. 3. Taking 1 Action requires pass; taking none or unable to act must pass. Empty hand after 2 Actions does not automatically pass; next round declaration required. 4. Player Phase ends when all players have passed, then Event Phase begins.
b.reader_evidence: 1. “Series of rounds repeat as long as at least one player has not passed.” 2. “starting with the First Player and going clockwise”; “round of 2 Actions.” 3. “If you perform only 1 Action … you must pass”; “If you cannot perform any Actions … must pass”; empty hand “does not automatically pass you.” 4. Event Airlock condition resolves when “all players passed”; Player Reference: rounds continue “until all players pass.”
b.expected_answer: Starting with the First Player, proceed clockwise, each active player taking a round of 2 Actions. After everyone has had a round, repeat rounds in that order while at least one player has not passed. Taking only 1 Action requires passing; taking none or being unable to act requires passing. Players who have passed are skipped for ordinary later Actions in this Player Phase; the FAQ permits Interruption after passing. Begin the Event Phase only after all players have passed.
b.reason: The no-automatic-Event, First Player/clockwise/two-Action repetition, one/zero-Action pass and all-passed gate clauses are resolved. Neither answer nor evidence actually states that passed players skip ordinary further rounds/Actions, expressly required by the scope addendum. The reader checklist supplies no missing rule.
